Create Spatial Proximity and Weights Matrix

Source: R/create_weights.R
create_weights.Rd

Constructs spatial proximity, contiguity, and weight matrices (\(\mathbf{W}\)) from spatial data (sf polygon or point objects, coordinate matrices, or neighbor lists). Supports Queen and Rook contiguity, \(k\)-nearest neighbors (\(k\)-NN), distance bands, and inverse distance weighting (IDW), with automatic fallback handling for isolated islands and disconnected domains.

Usage

create_weights(
  data,
  method = c("queen", "rook", "knn", "distance", "idw"),
  style = c("W", "B", "C", "U", "minmax"),
  k = 4,
  d_max = NULL,
  alpha = 1,
  island_fallback = TRUE,
  k_fallback = 1,
  domain = NULL
)

Arguments

data

An sf polygon or point object, a numeric matrix or data frame of 2D coordinates (with columns x/y or longitude/latitude), or an spdep nb or listw object.

method

Character string specifying the spatial weight method:

  • "queen": Queen contiguity (sharing at least one vertex or boundary edge).

  • "rook": Rook contiguity (sharing a common linear boundary edge).

  • "knn": \(k\)-nearest neighbors based on centroid/point distances.

  • "distance": Distance band where domains within d_max are neighbors.

  • "idw": Inverse distance weighting \(w_{ij} = 1 / d_{ij}^\alpha\).

style

Character string specifying the normalization style:

  • "W": Row-standardized (row sums equal 1, default for SAR/SFH models).

  • "B": Binary adjacency (0/1 values, standard for INLA BYM2/Besag models).

  • "C": Globally standardized.

  • "U": Equal weighting (\(1 / m\)).

  • "minmax": Min-max spectral normalization (divided by largest eigenvalue).

k

Integer. Number of nearest neighbors when method = "knn" (default is 4).

d_max

Numeric. Distance threshold when method = "distance". If NULL, it is automatically set to the minimum distance ensuring no disconnected domains.

alpha

Numeric. Distance decay power for method = "idw" (default is 1).

island_fallback

Logical. If TRUE (default), disconnected domains or islands with zero contiguous neighbors are automatically connected to their nearest neighbor(s) based on centroid distance.

k_fallback

Integer. Number of nearest neighbors to connect for isolated islands when island_fallback = TRUE (default is 1).

domain

Optional vector, column name, or one-sided formula referencing domain IDs. If provided, used as row and column names for the resulting matrix.

Value

A square numeric matrix of class c("fastsae_weights", "matrix") of dimension \(m \times m\). Attributes include method, style, n_domains, n_islands, and call.

Details

When working with real administrative boundaries (such as Indonesian provinces, regencies, or municipalities), island regencies (e.g. Kepulauan Seribu, Natuna, Sabang, Mentawai, Sangihe) lack contiguous land borders. If island_fallback = TRUE, create_weights detects these zero-neighbor domains and connects each to its closest k_fallback neighbor(s) based on centroid distances, ensuring a connected spatial graph without computational singularities.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("spdep", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # North Carolina counties, an sf polygon data set shipped with 'sf'
  nc <- sf::st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)
  W_queen <- create_weights(nc, method = "queen", style = "W")
  W_knn <- create_weights(nc, method = "knn", k = 5, style = "W")
  W_bin <- create_weights(nc, method = "queen", style = "B")
  W_queen
}
#> 
#> ── Spatial Weights Matrix (fastsae) ────────────────────────────────────────────
#> • Dimensions: 100 x 100 domains
#> • Construction Method: QUEEN
#> • Standardization Style: "W" (Row-standardized)
#> • Sparsity: 95.1% zeros
#> 
#> Matrix preview (top-left 5x5):
#>        1      2      3 4 5
#> 1 0.0000 0.3333 0.0000 0 0
#> 2 0.3333 0.0000 0.3333 0 0
#> 3 0.0000 0.2000 0.0000 0 0
#> 4 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 0 0
#> 5 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 0 0
#> ... and 95 more rows/columns.

# Create spatial weights from 2D coordinates
coords <- matrix(runif(40), ncol = 2)
W_coord <- create_weights(coords, method = "knn", k = 3, style = "W")
dim(W_coord)
#> [1] 20 20
